predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the Sivas-Tokat-Niksar-Amasya plateau of central Anatolia, where the Danishmends 'established themselves' after Manzikert (1071)

predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: the same plateau, which Cliopatria still draws inside the Great Seljuk shape of 1085-1093

successors.name: Sultanate of Rum
successors.text: the Danishmend remnant: Sivas (1174), Malatya (1178) and the rest of 'the Danishmend lands' taken by Kilij Arslan II

ledger.x: 1075: the Danishmend emirate arises in central Anatolia.

ledger.cp: Zinnun (Dhu'l-Nun), Emir Gazi's elder son at Kayseri

ledger.x: 1155: Yağıbasan fails against Kilij Arslan II.
1174: the Sivas lands pass to the Sultanate.
1178: Malatya is occupied and Danishmend rule ends.

wars.name: Danishmend capture of Bohemond of Antioch
wars.outcome: Emir Gazi captured Bohemond I of Antioch in 1100 and held him until 1103; no border moved.

wars.name: Crusade of 1101
wars.outcome: A Seljuk-Danishmend alliance defeated the Crusade of 1101 (Kilij Arslan I 'defeated three Crusade contingents'); the Danishmends take Malatya in September 1101.

wars.name: Danishmend-Antioch war of 1130
wars.outcome: Bohemond II of Antioch was killed in battle with Emir Gazi in 1130; no border moved.

wars.name: Danishmend-Rum wars
wars.outcome: Mesud I takes Sivas (1150) and Yağıbasan becomes a vassal; Yağıbasan is beaten at Aksaray by Kilij Arslan II (1155) but takes Elbistan with Byzantine help; the Sultanate absorbs the Sivas lands (1174), Nasreddin Muhammed is a Seljuk vassal (1175) and Malatya…

certainty.note: The Danishmend emirates of Niksar, Sivas, Kayseri and Malatya shared and exchanged land (1142 division, 1146 deposition of Zinnun); no frontier with Rum, Byzantium or the Crusader states is fixed on any page opened.
